Source: Fact A in the parent proof's conventions (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}), proved here in full.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
- For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}).
- I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P = Fin n ↪o Fin P, a finite type.
- For β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. (Kronecker property.) Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
(a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective). So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
(b) If β ≠ γ, there is i with β(i) ∉ {γ(0),…,γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ. Both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). An order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. (Agreement on increasing tuples.) Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. (Agreement on injective tuples.) Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. (Conclusion.) Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
5. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–4 cover them. For n = 0, I(0,P) has one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 4 gives α = 0 = R. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^β(e_γ) = det[δ_{β(i)γ(j)}] = δ_{βγ} for increasing β, γ.
R := Σ_β α(e_β)dx^β agrees with α on increasing basis tuples.
Sorting an injective tuple (Tuple.sort, AlternatingMap.map_perm) gives agreement on all injective basis tuples.
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives α = R.

subproblems.title: A smooth mollifier sequence whose mollifications converge a.e. for every locally integrable function
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ. There are functions ψ_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) such that for every k: ψ_k is C^∞; ψ_k has compact support; spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0), where spt is the closed support (Lean: tsupport); ψ_k ≥ 0; and ∫ ψ_k dLⁿ = 1. Moreover, for every locally Lⁿ-integrable g : ℝⁿ → ℝ, (g ∗ ψ_k)(x) := ∫ g(t) ψ_k(x − t) dLⁿ(t) → g(x) as k → ∞, for Lⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝⁿ. Here ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure (volume), and (g ∗ ψ_k)(x) is Lean's convolution g (ψ k) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x.

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source. Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34, printed proof p. 143: the mollifier ϕ_(σ)(x) = σ^{−n} ϕ(σ^{−1}x), with ϕ a mollifier as in §2 of Ch. 2 (printed p. 49: ϕ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ), ϕ ≥ 0, spt ϕ ⊆ B_1(0), ∫ϕ = 1). The printed proof concludes that θ_ε is constant on B_ρ(x₀) “letting σ ↓ 0”; this limiting fact is quoted in the bracket of Step 5 of the parent proof (“letting σ ↓ 0 (Lebesgue differentiation)”). Here σ = 1/(k+1). The a.e. convergence is derived from the Lebesgue differentiation theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17) in its Lebesgue-point form.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Eucl n; Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (volume); |·| is the Euclidean norm; B_s(x) = ball x s, B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s; spt = tsupport; ⨍_K f := Lⁿ(K)⁻¹ ∫_K f; (g ∗ ψ)(x) = ∫ g(t) ψ(x − t) dLⁿ(t) = convolution g ψ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x.

Proof.

1. (A fixed mollifier.) B_1(0) is a neighbourhood of 0, so there is a C^∞ function h : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support, spt h ⊆ B_1(0), 0 ≤ h ≤ 1 and h(0) = 1 (a smooth bump function).
- h is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Put I := ∫ h dLⁿ.
- The set {h ≠ 0} is open (h is continuous) and contains 0, so it has positive Lebesgue measure. Since h ≥ 0 is integrable, I > 0.
- If |y| ≥ 1 then y ∉ B_1(0) ⊇ spt h, so h(y) = 0.

2. (The kernels.) For k ∈ ℕ let s_k := k + 1 > 0, r_k := 1/s_k and ψ_k(y) := s_kⁿ · I⁻¹ · h(s_k y).
(a) ψ_k is C^∞: it is a constant multiple of h composed with the linear map y ↦ s_k y.
(b) If |y| ≥ r_k then |s_k y| = s_k|y| ≥ 1, so h(s_k y) = 0 and ψ_k(y) = 0. Hence {ψ_k ≠ 0} ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0). Since this ball is closed, spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0) = B̄_{1/(k+1)}(0).
(c) spt ψ_k is a closed subset of the compact ball B̄_{r_k}(0), so ψ_k has compact support.
(d) 0 ≤ ψ_k(y) ≤ s_kⁿ I⁻¹ for every y, since 0 ≤ h ≤ 1 and I > 0.
(e) ∫ ψ_k dLⁿ = s_kⁿ I⁻¹ ∫ h(s_k y) dy = s_kⁿ I⁻¹ · s_k^{−n} ∫ h dLⁿ = 1. This uses the linear change of variables ∫ f(R y) dy = |R|^{−n} ∫ f for R ≠ 0 (the dimension of ℝⁿ is n).
(f) ψ_k is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Since Lⁿ is invariant under translations and under y ↦ −y, for every x the function t ↦ ψ_k(x − t) is integrable and ∫ ψ_k(x − t) dt = ∫ ψ_k = 1.
(a)–(e) prove the first five assertions.

3. (Lebesgue points.) Let g be locally integrable. By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem in Lebesgue-point form, for Lⁿ-a.e. x:
 (∗) ⨍_{B̄_r(x)} |g(t) − g(x)| dt → 0 as r ↓ 0.
[Derivation from Simon 1.3.17. For each rational q, apply 3.17 to the locally integrable function |g − q|: ⨍_{B_r(x)} |g − q| → |g(x) − q| for x outside an Lⁿ-null set N_q. Let x ∉ ⋃_{q∈ℚ} N_q and q ∈ ℚ. Then ⨍_{B_r(x)} |g − g(x)| ≤ ⨍_{B_r(x)} |g − q| + |q − g(x)|, so limsup_{r↓0} ⨍_{B_r(x)} |g − g(x)| ≤ 2|g(x) − q|, which can be made arbitrarily small. Open and closed balls differ by a null sphere. Mathlib states (∗) directly as IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, since Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is uniformly locally doubling.]
Fix x satisfying (∗). Since r_k > 0 and r_k → 0, A_k := ⨍_{B̄_{r_k}(x)} |g(t) − g(x)| dt → 0 as k → ∞.

4. (The basic estimate.) Fix k and put K := B̄_{r_k}(x), a compact set.
(a) t ↦ g(t) ψ_k(x − t) is integrable. It vanishes off K, because ψ_k(x − t) = 0 when |x − t| ≥ r_k (2(b)). On K it is the product of g, which is integrable on the compact set K, with the bounded continuous function t ↦ ψ_k(x − t). (Mathlib: HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_right.)
(b) By 2(f), t ↦ g(x) ψ_k(x − t) is integrable with integral g(x).
(c) Hence (g ∗ ψ_k)(x) − g(x) = ∫ g(t) ψ_k(x − t) dt − ∫ g(x) ψ_k(x − t) dt = ∫ (g(t) − g(x)) ψ_k(x − t) dt.
(d) Since ψ_k ≥ 0: |∫ (g(t) − g(x)) ψ_k(x − t) dt| ≤ ∫ |g(t) − g(x)| ψ_k(x − t) dt.
(e) If t ∉ K then |x − t| > r_k, so ψ_k(x − t) = 0 by 2(b). Hence ∫ |g(t) − g(x)| ψ_k(x − t) dt = ∫_K |g(t) − g(x)| ψ_k(x − t) dt.
(f) t ↦ |g(t) − g(x)| is integrable on K, because g is integrable on K and constants are integrable on the finite-measure set K. By 2(d), 0 ≤ |g(t) − g(x)| ψ_k(x − t) ≤ s_kⁿ I⁻¹ |g(t) − g(x)|. Hence ∫_K |g(t) − g(x)| ψ_k(x − t) dt ≤ s_kⁿ I⁻¹ ∫_K |g(t) − g(x)| dt.
(g) By the scaling of Lebesgue measure, Lⁿ(K) = r_kⁿ ω with ω := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞). Since s_kⁿ r_kⁿ = 1, s_kⁿ = ω/Lⁿ(K). So s_kⁿ I⁻¹ ∫_K |g(t) − g(x)| dt = I⁻¹ ω ⨍_K |g(t) − g(x)| dt = C A_k, where C := I⁻¹ ω does not depend on k or x.
Altogether, |(g ∗ ψ_k)(x) − g(x)| ≤ C A_k for every k.

5. (Conclusion.) 0 ≤ |(g ∗ ψ_k)(x) − g(x)| ≤ C A_k, and C A_k → 0 by Step 3, so (g ∗ ψ_k)(x) → g(x) as k → ∞ (squeeze). This holds for every x satisfying (∗), i.e. for Lⁿ-a.e. x. This proves the last assertion. ∎
(For n = 0 every step holds verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point carrying the unit point mass, B_1(0) = ℝ⁰ and ω = 1.)

By Rademacher's theorem (`LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`), F is differentiable at λ^P-a.e. z ∈ ℝ^P.    - Φ(x′, y) := ρ(y)F(x′ − y),

   - b(y) := L·|ρ(y)|.

   (b) If ρ(y) ≠ 0, then |y| < σ, since |y| ≥ σ would force ρ(y) = 0. The Lipschitz property gives |F(x − y) − F(x)| ≤ L|(x − y) − x| = L|−y| = L|y| ≤ Lσ, using L ≥ 0. Since |ρ(y)| = ρ(y) ≥ 0, we get |ρ(y)(F(x − y) − F(x))| = ρ(y)|F(x − y) − F(x)| ≤ ρ(y)·(Lσ).

4. (Integrating the bound.) The majorant y ↦ ρ(y)·(Lσ) is integrable (step 1) and dominates |ρ(y)(F(x − y) − F(x))| for every y (step 3). Hence (`norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`)
   |∫ ρ(y)(F(x − y) − F(x)) dy| ≤ ∫ ρ(y)·(Lσ) dy = (∫ρ)·Lσ = Lσ (`integral_mul_const` and ∫ρ = 1).

5. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 2 and 4, |∫ ρ(y)F(x − y) dy − F(x)| ≤ Lσ. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every x ∈ ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: ρ and y ↦ ρ(y)F(x − y) are continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
Using ∫ρ = 1 and linearity: ∫ρ(y)F(x − y)dy − F(x) = ∫ρ(y)(F(x − y) − F(x))dy.
Pointwise |ρ(y)(F(x − y) − F(x))| ≤ ρ(y)·Lσ: ρ(y) ≠ 0 forces |y| < σ, and |F(x − y) − F(x)| ≤ L|y|.
norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the integrable majorant ρ·Lσ gives |…| ≤ Lσ·∫ρ = Lσ.

subproblems.title: Piola identity: the first-row cofactors of a Jacobian minor of C² functions are divergence-free (parent step (3.2)(i))
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ, let W_0, …, W_{r−1} : ℝ^k → ℝ (W : Fin r → (Eucl k → ℝ)) be of class C² (ContDiff ℝ 2), and let b : Fin (r+1) → Fin k. Write e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and ∂_i f(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (e_i). For q ∈ Fin (r+1) let c_q(x) := (−1)^q · det(∂_{b(q.succAbove s)} W_t(x))_{t,s ∈ Fin r}, where q.succAbove : Fin r → Fin (r+1) is the increasing enumeration of Fin (r+1) ∖ {q} (the empty determinant is 1). Then for every w ∈ ℝ^k: Σ_{q ∈ Fin (r+1)} fderiv ℝ c_q w (e_{b(q)}) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (W : Fin r → Eucl k → ℝ) (b : Fin (r + 1) → Fin k), (∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 2 (W t)) → ∀ w : Eucl k, ∑ q : Fin (r + 1), fderiv ℝ (fun x : Eucl k => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s : Fin r => fderiv ℝ (W t) x (EuclideanSpace.single (b (q.succAbove s)) 1))) w (EuclideanSpace.single (b q) 1) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (3.2)(i) of the parent proof (Piola identity: “Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}[C_q(v)] = 0 … H^t is symmetric in (q,s) (Schwarz's theorem, v ∈ C²) and D_t is antisymmetric in (q,s) (exchange of rows 0 and t), so every double sum vanishes”). Here the rows 1,…,r of the parent's minor are arbitrary C² scalar functions W_0,…,W_{r−1} (in the parent W_{t} = v^{a(t+1)} = proj_{a(t+1)} ∘ v), and the argument is written with the Leibniz expansion: the antisymmetry of the determinant under the exchange of rows 0 and t+1 is the sign change of a permutation σ under σ ↦ σ∘(0 t+1). Background: L. C. Evans, Partial Differential Equations, §8.1.4(b), Lemma 1 (divergence-free rows of cofactor matrices); J. M. Ball, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 63 (1977) 337–403.

Notation. ℝ^k = Eucl k; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; ∂_i f(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (e_i). For a C² function f and i, j ∈ Fin k put ∂_j∂_i f(x) := fderiv ℝ (y ↦ ∂_i f(y)) x (e_j). S_n := Equiv.Perm (Fin n), sgn := Equiv.Perm.sign. Leibniz formula in row form: det M = Σ_{σ∈S_n} sgn(σ) Π_i M_{i,σ(i)} (Mathlib Matrix.det_apply is the column form Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i M_{σ(i),i}; apply it to the transpose and use Matrix.det_transpose).

1. (Regularity and symmetry.) Fix t ∈ Fin r. Since W_t is C², fderiv ℝ W_t is C¹, so for each i the entry function x ↦ ∂_i W_t(x) = (fderiv ℝ W_t x)(e_i) is C¹ (composition with the continuous linear evaluation at e_i), and its derivative in the direction e_j is ∂_j∂_i W_t(x) = D²W_t(x)(e_j)(e_i), where D²W_t(x) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ W_t) x. By Schwarz's theorem for C² functions over ℝ (Mathlib ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt; minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2), D²W_t(x)(e_j)(e_i) = D²W_t(x)(e_i)(e_j). Hence ∂_j∂_i W_t = ∂_i∂_j W_t everywhere.

2. (Cofactor formula.) Fix x ∈ ℝ^k. For y ∈ ℝ^{Fin (r+1)} let A^y be the (r+1)×(r+1) matrix whose row 0 is y and whose row t.succ (t ∈ Fin r) is (∂_{b(s′)}W_t(x))_{s′ ∈ Fin (r+1)} (rows defined by Fin.cases).
 (a) Laplace expansion along row 0 (Mathlib Matrix.det_succ_row_zero): det A^y = Σ_{j∈Fin(r+1)} (−1)^j y_j det(A^y.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove), and the submatrix has entries (A^y.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove)_{t,s} = ∂_{b(j.succAbove s)}W_t(x). For y = 𝟙_q := Pi.single q 1 every term with j ≠ q vanishes, so det A^{𝟙_q} = (−1)^q det(∂_{b(q.succAbove s)}W_t(x))_{t,s} = c_q(x).
 (b) Leibniz formula: det A^{𝟙_q} = Σ_{σ∈S_{r+1}} sgn(σ)·(𝟙_q)_{σ(0)}·Π_{t∈Fin r} ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t(x) = Σ_{σ: σ(0)=q} sgn(σ) P_σ(x), where P_σ(x) := Π_{t∈Fin r} ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t(x) (the product over the rows of Fin (r+1) splits as row 0 times the rows t.succ, Fin.prod_univ_succ).
 Hence, as functions of x,
 c_q = Σ_{σ∈S_{r+1}, σ(0)=q} sgn(σ)·P_σ.  (1)

3. (Differentiation.) Each P_σ is a finite product of the C¹ functions of Step 1, hence differentiable, and by the product rule (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.finsetProd, fderiv_finsetProd), for every direction e_j:
 fderiv ℝ P_σ w (e_j) = Σ_{u∈Fin r} ∂_j∂_{b(σ(u.succ))}W_u(w) · Π_{t∈Fin r, t≠u} ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t(w).
 By (1) and linearity of the derivative, c_q is differentiable and fderiv ℝ c_q w (e_{b(q)}) = Σ_{σ: σ(0)=q} sgn(σ)·fderiv ℝ P_σ w (e_{b(q)}). Summing over q and grouping the permutations σ ∈ S_{r+1} according to the value σ(0) (every σ lies in exactly one fibre σ(0) = q, and in that fibre b(q) = b(σ(0)); Finset.sum_fiberwise):
 Σ_q fderiv ℝ c_q w (e_{b(q)}) = Σ_{σ∈S_{r+1}} sgn(σ)·fderiv ℝ P_σ w (e_{b(σ(0))}) = Σ_{u∈Fin r} S_u,
 where S_u := Σ_{σ∈S_{r+1}} T_u(σ), T_u(σ) := sgn(σ)·H_u(σ(0), σ(u.succ))·R_u(σ), with H_u(i, j) := ∂_{b(i)}∂_{b(j)}W_u(w) for i, j ∈ Fin (r+1) and R_u(σ) := Π_{t∈Fin r, t≠u} ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t(w).

4. (Cancellation.) Fix u ∈ Fin r and let τ := Equiv.swap 0 u.succ, a transposition because 0 ≠ u.succ (Fin.succ_ne_zero). Right multiplication σ ↦ σ*τ (that is, σ∘τ) is a bijection of S_{r+1} (Equiv.mulRight τ), so S_u = Σ_σ T_u(σ∘τ) (Equiv.sum_comp). For every σ:
 (a) sgn(σ∘τ) = sgn(σ)·sgn(τ) = −sgn(σ) (Equiv.Perm.sign_mul, Equiv.Perm.sign_swap);
 (b) (σ∘τ)(0) = σ(u.succ) and (σ∘τ)(u.succ) = σ(0) (Equiv.swap_apply_left, Equiv.swap_apply_right);
 (c) if t ≠ u then t.succ ≠ 0 and t.succ ≠ u.succ (Fin.succ_injective), so (σ∘τ)(t.succ) = σ(t.succ) (Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne), and therefore R_u(σ∘τ) = R_u(σ);
 (d) H_u(σ(u.succ), σ(0)) = H_u(σ(0), σ(u.succ)) by Step 1 (symmetry of the second derivative of W_u at w).
 Hence T_u(σ∘τ) = −T_u(σ) for every σ, so S_u = Σ_σ T_u(σ∘τ) = −Σ_σ T_u(σ) = −S_u, and S_u = 0.

5. (Conclusion.) Σ_{q∈Fin(r+1)} fderiv ℝ c_q w (e_{b(q)}) = Σ_{u∈Fin r} S_u = 0. The degenerate case r = 0 is included: then c_0 ≡ (−1)^0·det(0×0 matrix) = 1 is constant, so its derivative vanishes, in accordance with the empty sum over u ∈ Fin 0. (For k = 0 there is no map b : Fin (r+1) → Fin 0, so the statement is vacuous.) ∎

Every Mathlib name used above was checked to be available under the frozen `import GMT.Ch06.Submission` (do not add imports; the leaf gate rejects them): Matrix.det_succ_row_zero, Matrix.det_apply, Matrix.det_transpose, HasFDerivAt.finsetProd (the old name HasFDerivAt.finset_prod is a deprecated alias), fderiv_finsetProd, ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, Equiv.Perm.sign_mul, Equiv.Perm.sign_swap, Equiv.mulRight, Equiv.sum_comp, Finset.sum_involution. In Lean the sign is (-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) and the entry derivative is fderiv ℝ (fun y => fderiv ℝ (W t) y (e_i)) x (e_j) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (W t)) x (e_j) (e_i) (fderiv of the evaluation of a C¹ family of continuous linear maps at a constant vector).
proof_key_steps: Schwarz: the entries ∂_iW_t are C¹ and ∂_j∂_iW_t = ∂_i∂_jW_t (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt).
Cofactor formula from Laplace (det_succ_row_zero) and Leibniz expansions of the matrix with row 0 = 𝟙_q: c_q = Σ_{σ(0)=q} sgn(σ) Π_t ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t.
Product rule and regrouping by σ(0): Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}c_q = Σ_u Σ_σ sgn(σ) H_u(σ(0), σ(u.succ)) Π_{t≠u} ∂_{b(σ(t.succ))}W_t.
For each u the involution σ ↦ σ∘swap(0, u.succ) flips the sign, swaps the arguments of the symmetric H_u and fixes the other factors, so each inner sum is 0.

subproblems.title: Integration by parts for Jacobian minors of C² functions against a C¹ compactly supported test function (parent step (3.2)(ii))
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ, let V_0, …, V_r : ℝ^k → ℝ (V : Fin (r+1) → (Eucl k → ℝ)) be of class C², let b : Fin (r+1) → Fin k, and let φ : ℝ^k → ℝ be of class C¹ with compact support. With ∂_i f(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1), A(w) := (∂_{b(s)}V_t(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin (r+1)} and C_q(w) := (−1)^q det(∂_{b(q.succAbove s)}V_{t.succ}(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin r} for q ∈ Fin (r+1): ∫_{ℝ^k} φ(w)·det A(w) dw = −Σ_{q ∈ Fin (r+1)} ∫_{ℝ^k} V_0(w)·C_q(w)·∂_{b(q)}φ(w) dw, where dw is Lebesgue measure (volume).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (V : Fin (r + 1) → Eucl k → ℝ) (b : Fin (r + 1) → Fin k) (φ : Eucl k → ℝ), (∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 2 (V t)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ w, φ w * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s : Fin (r + 1) => fderiv ℝ (V t) w (EuclideanSpace.single (b s) 1)) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)) = -∑ q : Fin (r + 1), ∫ w, V 0 w * ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s : Fin r => fderiv ℝ (V t.succ) w (EuclideanSpace.single (b (q.succAbove s)) 1))) * fderiv ℝ φ w (EuclideanSpace.single (b q) 1) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (3.2)(ii) of the parent proof (“By (i), M_{a,b}(v) = Σ_q[∂_{b(q)}v^{a(0)}·C_q(v) + v^{a(0)}·∂_{b(q)}C_q(v)] = Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}(v^{a(0)}C_q(v)) near K. Multiplying by φ and integrating by parts in the direction e_{b(q)} … gives (P)”), for C² rows V_t (in the parent V_t = v^{a(t)}) defined on all of ℝ^k. The integration by parts is performed on the compactly supported function V_0·φ·C_q, so no boundary terms occur.

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ^k = Eucl k (volume); e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; ∂_i f(w) := fderiv ℝ f w (e_i); K := tsupport φ, a compact set.

1. (Laplace expansion.) For every w, Mathlib Matrix.det_succ_row_zero gives det A(w) = Σ_q (−1)^q A_{0q}(w) det(A(w).submatrix Fin.succ q.succAbove), and the submatrix has entries A_{t.succ, q.succAbove s}(w) = ∂_{b(q.succAbove s)}V_{t.succ}(w). Since A_{0q} = ∂_{b(q)}V_0, this reads det A(w) = Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}V_0(w)·C_q(w).

2. (Regularity.) Since V_t is C², each entry w ↦ ∂_iV_t(w) is C¹ (fderiv ℝ V_t is C¹; evaluate at the constant vector e_i). By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), C_q is a finite sum of ± products of such entries, hence C¹. V_0 is C² and φ is C¹, so ∂_iφ is continuous.

3. (Supports and integrability.) φ vanishes outside K, and so does each ∂_iφ: if w ∉ K, then φ vanishes on the open neighbourhood Kᶜ of w, so fderiv ℝ φ w = 0 (Mathlib support_fderiv_subset). Hence each of the functions φ·det A, V_0·C_q·∂_{b(q)}φ, ∂_{b(q)}V_0·φ·C_q and V_0·φ·∂_{b(q)}C_q (where ∂_{b(q)}C_q(w) = fderiv ℝ C_q w (e_{b(q)})) is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set K; so each has compact support and is λ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).

4. (A directional derivative of a compactly supported C¹ function has integral 0.) Let h : ℝ^k → ℝ be C¹ with compact support and e ∈ ℝ^k. Then ∫ fderiv ℝ h w (e) dλ(w) = 0.
 Proof. h is Lipschitz (Mathlib ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport, with n = 1 ≠ 0). The constant function f :≡ 1 is Lipschitz with constant 0. Mathlib's integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq in the Rademacher file; λ is an additive Haar measure on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^k) gives ∫ lineDeriv ℝ f w e · h(w) dλ = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ h w (−e) · f(w) dλ. The left side is 0, because the line derivative of a constant function is 0 (unfold lineDeriv: the derivative of the constant t ↦ 1 is 0). On the right, h is differentiable, so lineDeriv ℝ h w (−e) = fderiv ℝ h w (−e) = −fderiv ℝ h w (e) (DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv and linearity). Hence −∫ fderiv ℝ h w (e) dλ = 0. [Equivalent route: ∫ h(w + te) dλ(w) = ∫ h dλ for all t by translation invariance (integral_add_right_eq_self); differentiating at t = 0 under the integral sign (hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) gives the claim.]

5. (One integration by parts for each q.) Fix q and put h_q := V_0·φ·C_q. It is C¹ (Step 2) and vanishes outside K, so it has compact support. By the product rule, fderiv ℝ h_q w (e_{b(q)}) = ∂_{b(q)}V_0(w)·φ(w)·C_q(w) + V_0(w)·∂_{b(q)}φ(w)·C_q(w) + V_0(w)·φ(w)·∂_{b(q)}C_q(w). Integrating over ℝ^k, using Step 4 for h_q and e = e_{b(q)}, and linearity of the integral (all three terms are integrable by Step 3):
 ∫ ∂_{b(q)}V_0·φ·C_q dλ = −∫ V_0·C_q·∂_{b(q)}φ dλ − ∫ V_0·φ·∂_{b(q)}C_q dλ.

6. (Summation and the Piola identity.) By Step 1 and linearity (finite sum of integrable functions, Step 3),
 ∫ φ det A dλ = Σ_q ∫ ∂_{b(q)}V_0·φ·C_q dλ = −Σ_q ∫ V_0·C_q·∂_{b(q)}φ dλ − ∫ V_0·φ·(Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}C_q) dλ.
 The sibling piola_identity, applied to the C² rows W_t := V_{t.succ} (t ∈ Fin r) and the same b, states Σ_q fderiv ℝ C_q w (e_{b(q)}) = 0 for every w (its c_q is exactly our C_q, since W t = V t.succ). So the last integrand vanishes identically and
 ∫ φ(w)·det A(w) dλ(w) = −Σ_q ∫ V_0(w)·C_q(w)·∂_{b(q)}φ(w) dλ(w),
 which is the claim; in Lean the right-hand integrand is V 0 w * ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) * Matrix.det (…)) * fderiv ℝ φ w (EuclideanSpace.single (b q) 1). ∎ (For k = 0 there is no b : Fin (r+1) → Fin 0, so the statement is vacuous.)

proof_key_steps: Laplace expansion along row 0: det A = Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}V_0·C_q.
All integrands are continuous and supported in tsupport φ (fderiv φ vanishes off tsupport φ), hence integrable.
∫ ∂_e h = 0 for C¹ compactly supported h (LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq with f ≡ 1).
Apply it to h_q = V_0·φ·C_q in direction e_{b(q)} and expand by the product rule.
Sum over q; the sibling piola_identity (W_t := V_{t.succ}) kills Σ_q ∂_{b(q)}C_q, leaving −Σ_q ∫ V_0·C_q·∂_{b(q)}φ.

subproblems.title: Smooth approximation of a Lipschitz function with almost-everywhere convergent derivatives (mollification, parent step (3.2)(iii))
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 and let g : ℝ^k → ℝ (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be L-Lipschitz. Then there are functions G_m : ℝ^k → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) such that: every G_m is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order, not analytic); every G_m is L-Lipschitz; G_m → g uniformly on ℝ^k; and for Lebesgue-a.e. w ∈ ℝ^k, fderiv ℝ G_m w → fderiv ℝ g w in ℝ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ as m → ∞ (fderiv ℝ g w is the Fréchet derivative, 0 where g is not differentiable).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : ℝ≥0) (g : Eucl k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L g → ∃ G : ℕ → Eucl k → ℝ, (∀ m, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (G m)) ∧ (∀ m, LipschitzWith L (G m)) ∧ TendstoUniformly G g atTop ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)), Tendsto (fun m => fderiv ℝ (G m) w) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ g w))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (3.2)(iii) of the parent proof (“Let ρ_δ (0 < δ < d) be a standard mollifier … and v_δ := ρ_δ * ṽ componentwise. Then v_δ is C^∞; v_δ → ṽ uniformly on ℝ^k as δ → 0 …; ∂_bv_δ = ρ_δ * ∂_bṽ (differentiate under the integral sign …), hence |∂_bv_δ^a| ≤ C; and ∂_bv_δ → ∂_bṽ a.e. along any sequence δ_m → 0 (Lebesgue differentiation for mollifiers)”), for one scalar coordinate function g = ṽ^a and δ_m = 1/(m+1). The three analytic facts are supplied by the reused, comparator-accepted siblings ae_mollifier (kernels and Lebesgue differentiation), mollify_close (uniform error) and mollify_fderiv (differentiation under the integral sign).

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ^k (volume); e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1; Dg(w) := fderiv ℝ g w; for f, ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ, (f ∗ ψ)(x) := ∫ f(t)ψ(x − t) dλ(t) = convolution f ψ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x.

1. (Kernels.) Let ψ_m (m ∈ ℕ) be the functions given by the sibling ae_mollifier for n := k: each ψ_m is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ψ_m ⊆ closedBall 0 (1/(m+1)), ψ_m ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_m dλ = 1, and for every locally integrable f : ℝ^k → ℝ, (f ∗ ψ_m)(x) → f(x) as m → ∞ for λ-a.e. x. If ‖y‖ ≥ 2/(m+1) then y ∉ closedBall 0 (1/(m+1)) ⊇ tsupport ψ_m, so ψ_m(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).

2. (Definition.) Put G_m(x) := ∫ ψ_m(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y). For each x the integrand is continuous and vanishes where ψ_m does, so it has compact support and is integrable. By the definition of the convolution (convolution_def; lsmul ℝ ℝ a c = a·c), G_m = convolution ψ_m g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.

3. (Smoothness.) g is continuous (being Lipschitz), hence locally integrable; ψ_m is C^∞ with compact support. Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left (λ is invariant under translations and under negation) shows that ψ_m ⋆ g = G_m is C^∞, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) G_m.

4. (Lipschitz constant L.) For x, x′ ∈ ℝ^k, by linearity G_m(x) − G_m(x′) = ∫ ψ_m(y)(g(x − y) − g(x′ − y)) dλ(y), and |ψ_m(y)(g(x − y) − g(x′ − y))| ≤ ψ_m(y)·L‖(x − y) − (x′ − y)‖ = ψ_m(y)·L‖x − x′‖ because ψ_m ≥ 0. Integrating this bound (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le) and using ∫ψ_m = 1 gives |G_m(x) − G_m(x′)| ≤ L‖x − x′‖. So G_m is L-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).

5. (Uniform convergence.) Apply the sibling mollify_close with P := k, F := g, ρ := ψ_m and σ := 2/(m+1): ρ is continuous with compact support, ρ ≥ 0, ρ(y) = 0 whenever σ ≤ ‖y‖ (Step 1), and ∫ρ = 1. It yields |G_m(x) − g(x)| ≤ L·2/(m+1) for every x ∈ ℝ^k. Since 2L/(m+1) → 0, G_m → g uniformly on ℝ^k (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff).

6. (Derivative of G_m.) Apply the sibling mollify_fderiv with P := k, F := g, ρ := ψ_m (continuous, compact support): for every x, G_m has Fréchet derivative ∫ ψ_m(y)·Dg(x − y) dλ(y) at x (a Bochner integral in ℝ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ); hence fderiv ℝ G_m x = ∫ ψ_m(y)·Dg(x − y) dλ(y) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). The integrand y ↦ ψ_m(y)·Dg(x − y) is a.e.-strongly measurable (measurable_fderiv composed with y ↦ x − y), has norm ≤ L·ψ_m(y) (‖Dg‖ ≤ L by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz) and vanishes outside tsupport ψ_m, so it is integrable; therefore evaluation at a fixed vector e commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply). With h_e(t) := Dg(t)(e) and the measure-preserving substitution t = x − y (integral_sub_left_eq_self):
 fderiv ℝ G_m x (e) = ∫ ψ_m(y)·h_e(x − y) dλ(y) = ∫ h_e(t)·ψ_m(x − t) dλ(t) = (h_e ∗ ψ_m)(x).

7. (a.e. convergence of the partial derivatives.) h_e is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const) and |h_e| ≤ L‖e‖, so h_e is locally integrable. By ae_mollifier, (h_e ∗ ψ_m)(x) → h_e(x) = Dg(x)(e) for λ-a.e. x. Apply this to the finitely many vectors e = e_b (b ∈ Fin k) and intersect the full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for λ-a.e. x, fderiv ℝ G_m x (e_b) → Dg(x)(e_b) for every b ∈ Fin k.

8. (Operator-norm convergence.) For T : ℝ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ and z ∈ ℝ^k write z = Σ_b z_b e_b with |z_b| ≤ ‖z‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le); then |Tz| ≤ Σ_b |z_b||Te_b| ≤ (Σ_b |Te_b|)‖z‖, so ‖T‖ ≤ Σ_b |Te_b| (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). For x as in Step 7 and T := fderiv ℝ G_m x − Dg(x) this gives ‖fderiv ℝ G_m x − Dg(x)‖ ≤ Σ_b |fderiv ℝ G_m x (e_b) − Dg(x)(e_b)| → 0. Hence fderiv ℝ G_m x → fderiv ℝ g x for λ-a.e. x.

9. (Conclusion.) The sequence (G_m) has the four required properties (Steps 3, 4, 5 and 8). ∎ (For k = 0 every step applies verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, and ae_mollifier covers n = 0.)

subproblems.title: Integration by parts for Jacobian minors of maps Lipschitz on an open set: identity (P) of parent step (3.2)
subproblems.statement: Let k, Q, r ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, C ≥ 0, v : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q C-Lipschitz on Ω, a : Fin (r+1) → Fin Q, b : Fin (r+1) → Fin k, and φ : ℝ^k → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω. Write e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, v^c := EuclideanSpace.proj c ∘ v and ∂_iv^c(w) := EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w (e_i)) (Mathlib fderiv, 0 where v is not differentiable). Let M(w) := det(∂_{b(s)}v^{a(t)}(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin (r+1)} and C_q(w) := (−1)^q det(∂_{b(q.succAbove s)}v^{a(t.succ)}(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin r} for q ∈ Fin (r+1). Then ∫_Ω φ(w)·M(w) dw = −Σ_{q ∈ Fin (r+1)} ∫_Ω v^{a(0)}(w)·C_q(w)·fderiv ℝ φ w (e_{b(q)}) dw, where dw is Lebesgue measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k Q r : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)) (C : ℝ≥0) (a : Fin (r + 1) → Fin Q) (b : Fin (r + 1) → Fin k) (v : Eucl k → Eucl Q) (φ : Eucl k → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → LipschitzOnWith C v Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ Ω → ∫ w in Ω, φ w * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s : Fin (r + 1) => EuclideanSpace.proj (a t) (fderiv ℝ v w (EuclideanSpace.single (b s) 1))) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)) = -∑ q : Fin (r + 1), ∫ w in Ω, EuclideanSpace.proj (a 0) (v w) * ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s : Fin r => EuclideanSpace.proj (a t.succ) (fderiv ℝ v w (EuclideanSpace.single (b (q.succAbove s)) 1)))) * fderiv ℝ φ w (EuclideanSpace.single (b q) 1) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (3.2)(iii) of the parent proof (“Extend each coordinate v^a|_Ω to a C-Lipschitz function ṽ^a on ℝ^k (McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) … Apply (ii) to v_{δ_m} and let m → ∞: on K the integrands … converge a.e. … and are bounded by r!C^r|φ| and (sup_K|ṽ| + 1)(r−1)!C^{r−1}|∂_{b(q)}φ| … dominated convergence gives (P) for ṽ. Since ṽ = v on Ω and Dṽ = Dv a.e. on K ⊆ Ω, (P) holds for v.”). The smoothing v_{δ_m} is done coordinatewise by the sibling lipschitz_smooth_approx, and (ii) is the sibling minor_ibp_smooth applied to the smoothed coordinate rows. (The parent's r is our r+1.)

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure (volume); K := tsupport φ, compact with K ⊆ Ω; for scalar f, ∂_if(w) := fderiv ℝ f w (e_i); dφ_q := ∂_{b(q)}φ. For a family of scalar rows V : Fin (r+1) → (ℝ^k → ℝ) put M[V](w) := det(∂_{b(s)}V_t(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin (r+1)} and C_q[V](w) := (−1)^q det(∂_{b(q.succAbove s)}V_{t.succ}(w))_{t,s ∈ Fin r}.

1. (Coordinate extensions.) For c ∈ Fin Q, v^c is C-Lipschitz on Ω: |v^c(x) − v^c(y)| = |(v(x) − v(y))_c| ≤ ‖v(x) − v(y)‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le). By McShane's extension (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) there is ṽ^c : ℝ^k → ℝ, C-Lipschitz on all of ℝ^k, with ṽ^c = v^c on Ω.

2. (Smoothing.) Apply the sibling lipschitz_smooth_approx to each ṽ^c (with L := C): there are G^c_m : ℝ^k → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) that are C^∞ — in particular C² (ContDiff.of_le; the term `(hG m).of_le (WithTop.coe_le_coe.2 le_top)` proving ContDiff ℝ 2 from ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) was compiled against the frozen import) — C-Lipschitz, with G^c_m → ṽ^c uniformly on ℝ^k and fderiv ℝ G^c_m w → fderiv ℝ ṽ^c w for every w outside a λ-null set N_c. Let N := ⋃_c N_c, a finite union of null sets (ae_all_iff). Since G^c_m and ṽ^c are C-Lipschitz on ℝ^k, ‖fderiv ℝ G^c_m w‖ ≤ C and ‖fderiv ℝ ṽ^c w‖ ≤ C for all w (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz); hence every entry satisfies |∂_iG^c_m(w)| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ G^c_m w‖·‖e_i‖ ≤ C, and likewise for ṽ^c.

3. (Smooth identity.) For m ∈ ℕ let V^m_t := G^{a(t)}_m (t ∈ Fin (r+1)), C² functions. The sibling minor_ibp_smooth (rows V^m, the same b and φ) gives, with integrals over ℝ^k,
 ∫ φ·M[V^m] dλ = −Σ_q ∫ V^m_0·C_q[V^m]·dφ_q dλ.  (S_m)
 Let Ṽ_t := ṽ^{a(t)}.

4. (Limits, bounds and measurability of the integrands.)
 (a) For w ∉ N, each entry ∂_{b(s)}V^m_t(w) = fderiv ℝ G^{a(t)}_m w (e_{b(s)}) tends to ∂_{b(s)}Ṽ_t(w) (evaluation at e_{b(s)} is continuous). The determinant is a continuous function of the entries (Continuous.matrix_det), so M[V^m](w) → M[Ṽ](w) and C_q[V^m](w) → C_q[Ṽ](w). Moreover V^m_0(w) → Ṽ_0(w) for every w (uniform convergence).
 (b) By the Leibniz formula and the triangle inequality, an n×n matrix whose entries are bounded by C in absolute value has |det| ≤ n!·C^n (prove this from Matrix.det_apply; Matrix.det_le is not imported). Hence |M[V^m](w)| ≤ (r+1)!C^{r+1} and |C_q[V^m](w)| ≤ r!C^r for all m and w. Choose m₀ with |G^{a(0)}_m(w) − ṽ^{a(0)}(w)| ≤ 1 for all w and all m ≥ m₀. For m ≥ m₀ and all w: |φ·M[V^m]| ≤ (r+1)!C^{r+1}·|φ| and |V^m_0·C_q[V^m]·dφ_q| ≤ (|Ṽ_0| + 1)·r!C^r·|dφ_q|. Both majorants are continuous and vanish outside K (dφ_q vanishes off tsupport φ by support_fderiv_subset), so they are integrable.
 (c) Measurability: for every function f, w ↦ fderiv ℝ f w (e_i) is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const); G^c_m, ṽ^c, φ and dφ_q are continuous. So all integrands are a.e.-strongly measurable.

5. (Passage to the limit.) By dominated convergence (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence, with the eventual bounds of 4(b) and the a.e. limits of 4(a)), the left side of (S_m) tends to ∫ φ·M[Ṽ] dλ and, for each q, ∫ V^m_0·C_q[V^m]·dφ_q dλ → ∫ Ṽ_0·C_q[Ṽ]·dφ_q dλ (then sum over the finitely many q, tendsto_finsetSum). Since (S_m) holds for every m, uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique) gives
 ∫ φ·M[Ṽ] dλ = −Σ_q ∫ Ṽ_0·C_q[Ṽ]·dφ_q dλ.  (S)

6. (Back to v on Ω.)
 (a) Let w ∈ Ω. Since Ω is an open neighbourhood of w on which ṽ^c = v^c, the two functions agree near w, so fderiv ℝ ṽ^c w = fderiv ℝ v^c w (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq) and ṽ^c(w) = v^c(w).
 (b) By Rademacher's theorem on Ω (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem; for w in the open set Ω, differentiability within Ω at w is differentiability at w, DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt), v is differentiable at λ-a.e. w ∈ Ω. At such w the chain rule for the continuous linear map EuclideanSpace.proj c gives fderiv ℝ v^c w = (EuclideanSpace.proj c).comp (fderiv ℝ v w) (fderiv_comp), hence ∂_iṽ^c(w) = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w (e_i)) = ∂_iv^c(w).
 Consequently, for λ-a.e. w ∈ Ω: M[Ṽ](w) = M(w), C_q[Ṽ](w) = C_q(w) and Ṽ_0(w) = v^{a(0)}(w); so the integrands of (S) agree λ-a.e. on Ω with φ·M and v^{a(0)}·C_q·dφ_q.
 (c) Outside K ⊆ Ω we have φ = 0 and dφ_q = 0, so the integrands of (S) vanish outside Ω. Therefore each integral over ℝ^k in (S) equals the integral of the same integrand over Ω (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and by (b) that integral equals the corresponding integral over Ω in the statement (setIntegral_congr_ae; Ω is measurable since it is open).
 Hence ∫_Ω φ·M dλ = −Σ_q ∫_Ω v^{a(0)}·C_q·dφ_q dλ, which is the claim (in Lean, EuclideanSpace.proj (a 0) (v w) * ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (q : ℕ) * Matrix.det (…)) * fderiv ℝ φ w (EuclideanSpace.single (b q) 1)). ∎ (For k = 0 there is no b : Fin (r+1) → Fin 0, so the statement is vacuous.)

subproblems.title: Test-function reduction for bounded sequences: convergence against C¹_c(Ω) implies convergence against L¹(Ω) (density of C_c^∞(Ω) in L¹(Ω), parent step (3.0))
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, B ∈ ℝ, and let f_j : ℝ^k → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) and f₀ : ℝ^k → ℝ be a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to Ω, with |f_j(w)| ≤ B and |f₀(w)| ≤ B for all j and all w ∈ Ω. Suppose that ∫_Ω φ(w)·f_j(w) dw → ∫_Ω φ(w)·f₀(w) dw as j → ∞ for every φ : ℝ^k → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω. Then ∫_Ω η(w)·f_j(w) dw → ∫_Ω η(w)·f₀(w) dw as j → ∞ for every η : ℝ^k → ℝ that is Lebesgue-integrable on Ω (dw = Lebesgue measure, volume).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (3.0) of the parent proof (“Smooth test functions suffice. Assume the convergence for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) … Given η integrable on Ω and ε > 0, choose φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) with ∫_Ω|η − φ| < ε (C_c^∞(Ω) is dense in L¹(Ω) …). By Step 0, |∫ηM_{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ηM_{a,b}(v)| ≤ 2·r!C^r·ε + |∫φ(M_{a,b}(v_j) − M_{a,b}(v))|, and the claim for η follows”), stated for an arbitrary sequence bounded by B in place of the minors and for the larger test class C¹ (a C^∞ approximant is in particular C¹). The density of compactly supported smooth functions in L¹(Ω) is proved by exhaustion, truncation and mollification with the reused, comparator-accepted sibling ae_mollifier (in place of the parent's “approximate by a continuous function with compact support and mollify”, since Mathlib's continuous-density file is not in the frozen import closure).

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ^k (volume); ∫_Ω = integral with respect to λ restricted to Ω; for f, ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ, (f ∗ ψ)(x) := ∫ f(t)ψ(x − t) dλ(t) = convolution f ψ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x.

1. (Density lemma.) Claim: for every η integrable on Ω and every ε > 0 there is a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^k → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω such that ∫_Ω |η − φ| dλ < ε. (A C^∞ function is C¹: `h.of_le (WithTop.coe_le_coe.2 le_top)` turns ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) into ContDiff ℝ 1; compiled against the frozen import.)
 (a) Exhaustion. For n ∈ ℕ let K_n := closedBall(0, n) ∩ (thickening(1/(n+1), Ωᶜ))ᶜ. It is closed (thickenings are open, Metric.isOpen_thickening) and bounded, hence compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). K_n ⊆ Ω, since a point of Ωᶜ lies in every positive thickening of Ωᶜ (Metric.self_subset_thickening). K_n ⊆ K_{n+1}. Every w ∈ Ω lies in K_n for all large n: choose ρ > 0 with ball(w, ρ) ⊆ Ω (Ω is open); if n ≥ ‖w‖ and 1/(n+1) ≤ ρ, then w ∉ thickening(1/(n+1), Ωᶜ), for otherwise some z ∈ Ωᶜ satisfies dist(w, z) < 1/(n+1) ≤ ρ, i.e. z ∈ ball(w, ρ) ⊆ Ω, a contradiction.
 (b) Truncation. For n ∈ ℕ put η_n(w) := 1_{K_n}(w)·max(−n, min(n, η(w))). Then |η_n| ≤ |η|, and η_n(w) → η(w) for every w ∈ Ω (for large n, w ∈ K_n and |η(w)| ≤ n). Each η_n is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Ω. By dominated convergence on Ω (majorant 2|η|, integrable on Ω), ∫_Ω |η − η_n| dλ → 0. Fix n with ∫_Ω |η − η_n| dλ < ε/2 and put h := η_n, K := K_n. Then h vanishes outside the compact set K ⊆ Ω and |h| ≤ n everywhere. Moreover h is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ on all of ℝ^k: it is the indicator of the measurable set K of the function max(−n, min(n, η)), which is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Ω and hence for λ restricted to K ⊆ Ω (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff). Consequently h is λ-integrable (bounded, with support in a set of finite measure), in particular locally integrable.
 (c) Mollification. Let ψ_m (m ∈ ℕ) be the kernels of the sibling ae_mollifier for n := k: ψ_m is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ψ_m ⊆ closedBall(0, 1/(m+1)), ψ_m ≥ 0, ∫ψ_m dλ = 1, and (f ∗ ψ_m)(x) → f(x) for λ-a.e. x whenever f is locally integrable. Put h_m := h ∗ ψ_m.
 (i) h_m is C^∞: Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right (ψ_m is C^∞ with compact support and h is locally integrable).
 (ii) Support. If x ∉ cthickening(1/(m+1), K), then for every t either t ∉ K, so h(t) = 0, or t ∈ K and ‖x − t‖ > 1/(m+1), so x − t ∉ tsupport ψ_m and ψ_m(x − t) = 0; hence h_m(x) = 0. So tsupport h_m ⊆ cthickening(1/(m+1), K), a closed set. Since K is compact and Ω is open, there is d > 0 with cthickening(d, K) ⊆ Ω (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and L := cthickening(d, K) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). For every m with 1/(m+1) ≤ d: tsupport h_m ⊆ L ⊆ Ω, so h_m has compact support.
 (iii) Bound. |h_m(x)| ≤ ∫ |h(t)|ψ_m(x − t) dλ(t) ≤ n·∫ ψ_m(x − t) dλ(t) = n, using ψ_m ≥ 0 and the invariance of λ under t ↦ x − t (integral_sub_left_eq_self).
 (iv) Convergence. h_m → h λ-a.e. (ae_mollifier applied to the locally integrable function h).
 (v) L¹ convergence. Let m₀ satisfy 1/(m₀+1) ≤ d. For m ≥ m₀ the function |h_m − h| vanishes outside L and is bounded by 2n, and 2n·1_L is integrable (L is compact). By (iv) and dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ |h_m − h| dλ → 0.
 Choose m ≥ m₀ with ∫ |h_m − h| dλ < ε/2 and put φ := h_m. Then φ is C^∞, has compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ Ω, and ∫_Ω |η − φ| ≤ ∫_Ω |η − h| + ∫_Ω |h − φ| ≤ ∫_Ω |η − h| + ∫ |h − φ| < ε.

2. (Integrability.) Let ζ be integrable on Ω (ζ = η, or ζ = φ from Step 1: φ is continuous with compact support, hence integrable). Since f_j and f₀ are a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Ω and bounded by B on Ω (hence a.e. for λ restricted to Ω), ζ·f_j and ζ·f₀ are integrable on Ω (Integrable.mul_bdd), and |∫_Ω ζ·f_j| ≤ B·∫_Ω|ζ|, |∫_Ω ζ·f₀| ≤ B·∫_Ω|ζ| (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).

3. (ε/3 argument.) Let η be integrable on Ω and δ > 0. If Ω = ∅ every integral is 0 and the sequence is constant. Otherwise B ≥ |f₀(w)| ≥ 0 for some w ∈ Ω, so B ≥ 0. Choose ε > 0 with 2Bε < δ/2, then φ by Step 1 with ∫_Ω|η − φ| < ε, and — by the hypothesis applied to this φ (C¹, compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ Ω) — an N such that |∫_Ω φ·f_j − ∫_Ω φ·f₀| < δ/2 for all j ≥ N. For j ≥ N, by linearity (Step 2),
 ∫_Ω η·f_j − ∫_Ω η·f₀ = ∫_Ω (η − φ)·f_j + (∫_Ω φ·f_j − ∫_Ω φ·f₀) − ∫_Ω (η − φ)·f₀,

subproblems.title: Weak-* convergence of all Jacobian minors of uniformly convergent, uniformly Lipschitz maps (the Claim of parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let k, Q ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, C ≥ 0, and let v_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q (j ∈ ℕ) and v₀ : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q all be C-Lipschitz on Ω with v_j → v₀ uniformly on Ω. For r ∈ ℕ, a : Fin r → Fin Q, b : Fin r → Fin k and u : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q let M_{a,b}(u)(w) := det(EuclideanSpace.proj (a t) (fderiv ℝ u w (EuclideanSpace.single (b s) 1)))_{t,s ∈ Fin r} (the r×r Jacobian minor with rows a and columns b; Mathlib fderiv, 0 where u is not differentiable; the empty determinant is 1). Then for every r, every a, b and every η : ℝ^k → ℝ that is Lebesgue-integrable on Ω: ∫_Ω η(w)·M_{a,b}(v_j)(w) dw → ∫_Ω η(w)·M_{a,b}(v₀)(w) dw as j → ∞ (dw = Lebesgue measure).

Source: the Claim of step 3 of the parent proof together with its proof (3.0)–(3.3): induction on the order r, for all a, b, η simultaneously; step (3.0) is the sibling test_density and the identity (P) of (3.2) is the sibling minor_ibp_lipschitz. This is the classical weak continuity of Jacobian minors in W^{1,∞} (J. M. Ball, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 63 (1977) 337–403; I. Fonseca, G. Leoni, J. Malý, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 178 (2005) 411–448).

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; u^c := EuclideanSpace.proj c ∘ u. For a : Fin (r+1) → Fin Q, b : Fin (r+1) → Fin k and q ∈ Fin (r+1) put a′ := (t ↦ a(t.succ)) : Fin r → Fin Q and b^{(q)} := (s ↦ b(q.succAbove s)) : Fin r → Fin k. Then the cofactor of the sibling minor_ibp_lipschitz is C_q(u) = (−1)^q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(u).

0. (Bounds and measurability.) Let u be C-Lipschitz on Ω and w ∈ Ω. Since Ω is a neighbourhood of w, ‖fderiv ℝ u w‖ ≤ C (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn). Hence every entry satisfies |EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ u w (e_i))| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ u w (e_i)‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ u w‖·‖e_i‖ ≤ C (PiLp.norm_apply_le, ‖e_i‖ = 1), and by the Leibniz formula and the triangle inequality |M_{a,b}(u)(w)| ≤ r!·C^r for w ∈ Ω (an n×n matrix with entries bounded by c has |det| ≤ n!·c^n; prove it from Matrix.det_apply, since Matrix.det_le is not imported). The function w ↦ M_{a,b}(u)(w) is Borel measurable: each entry is EuclideanSpace.proj c applied to the measurable function w ↦ fderiv ℝ u w (e_i) (measurable_fderiv_apply_const), and the determinant is continuous in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det on the function space, measurable_pi_iff). Also u is continuous on Ω (LipschitzOnWith.continuousOn).

We prove by induction on r the statement P(r): for all a : Fin r → Fin Q, b : Fin r → Fin k and all η integrable on Ω, ∫_Ω η·M_{a,b}(v_j) → ∫_Ω η·M_{a,b}(v₀).

1. (r = 0.) A 0×0 determinant equals 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty), so every term of the sequence equals ∫_Ω η: the sequence is constant.

2. (Step r → r+1: reduction to C¹ test functions.) Assume P(r) and fix a : Fin (r+1) → Fin Q and b : Fin (r+1) → Fin k. Apply the sibling test_density with f_j := M_{a,b}(v_j), f₀ := M_{a,b}(v₀) and B := (r+1)!·C^{r+1}: by Step 0 these functions are a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Ω and bounded by B on Ω. So it suffices to prove, for every φ : ℝ^k → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω,
 ∫_Ω φ·M_{a,b}(v_j) → ∫_Ω φ·M_{a,b}(v₀).  (★)

3. (Integration by parts.) Fix such φ, let K := tsupport φ (compact, K ⊆ Ω) and dφ_q(w) := fderiv ℝ φ w (e_{b(q)}). dφ_q is continuous (φ ∈ C¹) and vanishes outside K (support_fderiv_subset), hence it has compact support and is integrable. By the sibling minor_ibp_lipschitz, for u ∈ {v_j, v₀},
 ∫_Ω φ·M_{a,b}(u) = −Σ_{q∈Fin(r+1)} ∫_Ω u^{a(0)}·((−1)^q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(u))·dφ_q.
 Hence (★) follows (tendsto_finsetSum, Tendsto.neg) once we show, for each fixed q,
 I_j := ∫_Ω v_j^{a(0)}·((−1)^q M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j))·dφ_q → I_0 := ∫_Ω v₀^{a(0)}·((−1)^q M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v₀))·dφ_q.  (★★)

4. (Integrability.) Each u ∈ {v_j, v₀} is continuous on Ω ⊇ K, so |u^{a(0)}| ≤ P_u on the compact set K for some constant P_u ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Every function F used below is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Ω and satisfies |F(w)| ≤ c·|dφ_q(w)| for all w ∈ Ω with a constant c (on K use the bounds P_u and Step 0; off K, F(w) = 0 because F contains the factor dφ_q(w) = 0). Hence F is integrable on Ω (Integrable.mono′ with the integrable majorant c|dφ_q|). This applies to (v_j^{a(0)} − v₀^{a(0)})·((−1)^q M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j))·dφ_q (c = (P_{v_j} + P_{v₀})·r!C^r) and to η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(u) (c = P_{v₀}·r!C^r), where η_q := v₀^{a(0)}·dφ_q. In particular η_q itself is integrable on Ω (c = P_{v₀}).

5. (Splitting.) By linearity (Step 4),
 I_j = ∫_Ω (v_j^{a(0)} − v₀^{a(0)})·((−1)^q M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j))·dφ_q + (−1)^q·∫_Ω η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j), and I_0 = 0 + (−1)^q·∫_Ω η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v₀).

6. (First term → 0.) Let ε > 0, B′ := r!·C^r, I_φ := ∫ |dφ_q| dλ and δ := ε/(2(B′I_φ + 1)) > 0. By uniform convergence on Ω (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) there is N with ‖v_j(w) − v₀(w)‖ < δ for all j ≥ N and w ∈ Ω; then |v_j^{a(0)}(w) − v₀^{a(0)}(w)| ≤ ‖v_j(w) − v₀(w)‖ < δ (PiLp.norm_apply_le). Using |M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j)| ≤ B′ on Ω (Step 0), the first integrand is bounded on Ω by δB′|dφ_q|, so for j ≥ N the first integral has absolute value ≤ δB′I_φ < ε (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, setIntegral_le_integral). Hence it tends to 0.

7. (Second term: induction hypothesis.) P(r), applied to a′, b^{(q)} and the function η_q, which is integrable on Ω by Step 4, gives ∫_Ω η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v_j) → ∫_Ω η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v₀); multiplication by the constant (−1)^q preserves the limit.

8. (Conclusion of the step.) By Steps 5–7, I_j → 0 + (−1)^q·∫_Ω η_q·M_{a′,b^{(q)}}(v₀) = I_0, which is (★★). Hence (★) holds for every admissible φ, and Step 2 gives P(r+1). By induction P(r) holds for every r, which is the statement. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let k, Q, r ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ Lebesgue-integrable on Ω, g : ℝ^Q → ℝ continuous with compact support, C ≥ 0, and let u_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q (j ∈ ℕ) and u₀ : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q all be C-Lipschitz on Ω with u_j → u₀ uniformly on Ω; let a : Fin r → Fin Q and b : Fin r → Fin k. With M_{a,b}(u)(w) := det(EuclideanSpace.proj (a t) (fderiv ℝ u w (EuclideanSpace.single (b s) 1)))_{t,s ∈ Fin r} (Mathlib fderiv, 0 where u is not differentiable; the empty determinant is 1): ∫_Ω ψ(w)·g(u_j(w))·M_{a,b}(u_j)(w) dw → ∫_Ω ψ(w)·g(u₀(w))·M_{a,b}(u₀)(w) dw as j → ∞ (dw = Lebesgue measure).

Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the splitting into D₁(j) + D₂(j), with (a) the uniform-continuity estimate and (b) the Claim of step 3), for an arbitrary minor M_{a,b} and an arbitrary continuous compactly supported scalar coefficient g; in the parent, g = α_γ = (y ↦ euclideanCovectorCoordinate (α y) γ), r = k, a = γ and b = id. This is the estimate “∫ψ(ω_γ∘u_j)M_γ(Du_j) − ∫ψ(ω_γ∘u)M_γ(Du) = ∫ψ(ω_γ∘u_j − ω_γ∘u)M_γ(Du_j) + ∫ψ(ω_γ∘u)(M_γ(Du_j) − M_γ(Du)) → 0” quoted in the parent proof.

Notation. λ = Lebesgue measure; ∫_Ω = integral over Ω with respect to λ; M_j := M_{a,b}(u_j), M_0 := M_{a,b}(u₀); B := r!·C^r.

1. (Bounds and measurability.) For u ∈ {u_j, u₀} and w ∈ Ω: ‖fderiv ℝ u w‖ ≤ C (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn, since Ω ∈ 𝓝 w), so every entry of the minor has absolute value ≤ C (PiLp.norm_apply_le, ‖EuclideanSpace.single i 1‖ = 1) and |M_{a,b}(u)(w)| ≤ B (Leibniz formula and triangle inequality, from Matrix.det_apply). M_{a,b}(u) is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const; the determinant is continuous in the entries). g is continuous with compact support, so |g| ≤ G for a constant G (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support) and g is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). u is continuous on Ω (LipschitzOnWith.continuousOn), so g∘u is continuous on Ω and a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to the open, hence measurable, set Ω (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable).

2. (Integrability.) Put η := ψ·(g∘u₀). Since ψ is integrable on Ω and g∘u₀ is a.e.-strongly measurable on Ω and bounded by G, η is integrable on Ω (Integrable.mul_bdd). Likewise ψ·(g∘u_j − g∘u₀) is integrable on Ω (bounded by 2G|ψ|), and multiplying a function integrable on Ω by M_j or M_0 (measurable and bounded by B on Ω) keeps it integrable on Ω. In particular ψ·(g∘u_j)·M_j = ψ·(g∘u_j − g∘u₀)·M_j + η·M_j with both summands integrable on Ω.

3. (Splitting.) Hence ∫_Ω ψ·(g∘u_j)·M_j = D₁(j) + ∫_Ω η·M_j with D₁(j) := ∫_Ω ψ·(g∘u_j − g∘u₀)·M_j, while ∫_Ω ψ·(g∘u₀)·M_0 = 0 + ∫_Ω η·M_0.

4. (D₁(j) → 0.) Since g is uniformly continuous and u_j → u₀ uniformly on Ω, g∘u_j → g∘u₀ uniformly on Ω (UniformContinuous.comp_tendstoUniformlyOn). Let ε > 0, I := ∫_Ω |ψ| and δ := ε/(2(BI + 1)) > 0. There is N with |g(u_j(w)) − g(u₀(w))| < δ for all j ≥ N and w ∈ Ω (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). For such j, |ψ(w)·(g(u_j(w)) − g(u₀(w)))·M_j(w)| ≤ δB|ψ(w)| for w ∈ Ω, so |D₁(j)| ≤ δBI < ε (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). Thus D₁(j) → 0.

5. (Weak-* convergence.) The sibling minor_weak_star, applied to v := u (so v_j = u_j), v₀ := u₀, the same r, a, b and the function η, which is integrable on Ω by Step 2, gives ∫_Ω η·M_j → ∫_Ω η·M_0.

6. (Conclusion.) By Steps 3–5, ∫_Ω ψ·(g∘u_j)·M_j = D₁(j) + ∫_Ω η·M_j → 0 + ∫_Ω η·M_0 = ∫_Ω ψ·(g∘u₀)·M_0. ∎
